A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Latent Policy Barrier work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching the renumbered appendix ablations.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation benchmarks, real-robot Cup Arrangement and Belt Assembly experiments, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds an OOD-threshold sensitivity experiment on Transport and Tool-Hang in Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same diffusion policy, frozen encoder, rollout-trained latent dynamics model, and OOD-triggered gradient guidance. The new experiment varies an existing threshold without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Push-T, Square, Tool-Hang, Transport, Libero-10, Cup Arrangement, and Belt Assembly. The threshold sweep reuses existing tasks without introducing a new population, domain, or input-environment scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Expert BC, Mixed BC, Filtered BC, CCIL, and CQL. The data-source, action-optimization, and latent-representation comparators in Tables 2–4 are also unchanged after appendix renumbering.

E3.justification: New Figure 11 introduces a threshold-sweep evaluation: five OOD thresholds from 1.6 to 4.0 for Transport and from 0.8 to 2.0 for Tool-Hang. Previously reported evaluation settings and default thresholds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds Appendix A.2 and Figure 11 to test sensitivity to the OOD threshold. This supplements the retained guidance, data-source, action-optimization, and representation ablations with one focused analysis on two existing tasks.

E5.justification: Table 1's mean and standard deviation reporting over three checkpoints and Appendix B's checkpoint protocol are unchanged. Figure 11 uses the existing shaded-curve style without introducing a new uncertainty definition, run count, or statistical test.

E6.justification: Figure 11 adds success-rate curves that peak at thresholds 2.8 for Transport and 1.4 for Tool-Hang, with lower performance toward both extremes. Existing benchmark scores, earlier ablation results, and qualitative rollout findings are retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), including the dynamics loss, latent OOD score, and guidance rule, are unchanged. The added threshold analysis is empirical and introduces no mathematical definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about separating imitation from recovery, improving robustness and sample efficiency, and supporting pretrained policies. The additional ablation does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.2 attributes high-threshold performance drops to insufficient corrections and low-threshold drops to local optima that stall progress, particularly hook insertion in Tool-Hang. These specific failure-mode explanations are absent from v1; Section 5's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B and Tables 5–9 retain the same implementation descriptions, default hyperparameters, rollout schedules, hardware, training times, robot setups, and resource links. The added sensitivity experiment supplies no revised implementation or access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography, and the substantive comparisons with prior research are unchanged. The new appendix experiment adds no citations or novelty claims.

P1.justification: v2 corrects a few typos, clarifies the gradient-guidance heading in A.1, and inserts A.2 while renumbering later ablations. The first-page publication note changes to NeurIPS 2025; the main narrative remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel Figure 11, corrects the rollout labels in Figure 2, and fixes Figure 10's overlap with preceding text. Later appendix tables and paragraphs shift position, while their content and overall display structure are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 studies guidance strength and denoising steps but does not test the OOD activation threshold. v2 adds a focused two-task sensitivity study and explains how threshold extremes can impair recovery or stall progress, improving understanding of practical failure conditions. Small presentation fixes also improve readability. These are limited gains; the method and principal experimental evidence remain unchanged.
